identity: An enterprise data grid with column headers, rows, selection controls, and controls for finding, changing, and arranging records.

scenarios.name: sort
scenarios.screen: A table of about a dozen records shows labeled columns and sortable headers. The rows are in their initial order, no sort is active, and the header menus are closed.
never: A header already showing the requested sort direction

arrangements.text: The headers run across the top of the table, with rows directly beneath them.
The headers and rows keep the same grid order, while any table controls sit to the right above the headers.

scenarios.name: filter
scenarios.screen: A table of products or other records has a quick search box and column filter controls. About a dozen rows are visible; the search box is empty, no filter is applied, and every filter menu is closed.
never: A value already entered in quick search
Filter values already checked in an open menu
Only the goal rows shown before filtering

arrangements.text: The search box sits above the table, and filter controls sit in the column headers.
The search box sits beside the table's other controls above the right end of the headers; filter controls remain in the headers.

scenarios.name: paginate
scenarios.screen: A paged table shows one page of records with row checkboxes, a quick search box, page-size control, and a pager with Prev, page numbers, and Next. About a dozen rows appear on the first page, and no row is selected.
never: All records displayed on one page
A page other than the first already selected

arrangements.text: Search and page size sit above the table, with the pager below its rows.
Search sits above the left end of the table, page size above the right end, and the pager below the right end.

scenarios.name: select
scenarios.screen: A single page of about seven rows has a checkbox beside each row and a select-all checkbox in the header. All checkboxes start clear, and no selection action is open.

arrangements.text: The select-all checkbox heads the leftmost checkbox column, beside the table's data columns.
Selection controls sit above the table, while the checkbox column remains at the left of the rows.

scenarios.name: bulk
scenarios.screen: A single page of about seven rows has row checkboxes, a select-all checkbox, and toolbar actions for changing status, archiving, or deleting records. No row is selected, the status menu and confirmation dialog are closed, and there is no Undo toast.
never: A delete confirmation dialog already open
An Undo toast from an action

arrangements.text: Bulk actions sit above the table, and checkboxes form its leftmost column.
Bulk actions sit above the right end of the table, with the checkbox column at the left of the rows.

scenarios.name: resize
scenarios.screen: A table shows labeled columns at their initial widths and about a dozen records. The right edges of its headers are resize targets; no edge is being dragged.
never: A column already at its requested new width

arrangements.text: Column headers span the top of the table, with each resize edge between neighboring headers.
Table controls sit above the right end of the headers; the resize edges stay at the headers' right boundaries.

scenarios.name: reorder
scenarios.screen: A table of about a dozen records shows its columns in their initial order. Headers can be dragged to move columns, and no header is being dragged.
never: A header already detached for dragging
Columns already in the requested order

arrangements.text: The headers form one row above the records, with each column's cells directly below its header.
Table controls sit above the headers on the right; headers and their cells remain aligned in columns.

scenarios.name: multirow
scenarios.screen: A single page of about eight rows shows a table and toolbar bulk actions. Rows are selected by clicking their bodies rather than checkboxes; no row is selected and no action menu or confirmation dialog is open.

arrangements.text: Bulk actions sit above the table, whose full-width row bodies are the selection targets.
Bulk actions sit above the right end of the table, with selectable rows extending across the columns below.

scenarios.name: cellEdit
scenarios.screen: A single page of about six records shows ordinary text and number cells in their default order. No cell is being edited and no input field is open inside the table.
never: A draft value already typed into a cell

arrangements.text: Column headers sit above the rows, with editable values in cells directly below their headers.
Table controls sit above the right end of the grid; editable cells remain in the rows beneath the headers.

scenarios.name: crm
scenarios.screen: A ticket table shows named records with columns that include Owner and Subject. About six rows are visible, and every cell shows its saved value with no editor open.
never: An Owner or Subject cell already in edit mode

arrangements.text: Ticket headers run across the top, and each ticket occupies a row beneath them.
Table controls sit above the right end of the ticket grid; Owner and Subject values remain in their columns.

scenarios.name: colfilter
scenarios.screen: A ticket table has value-filter controls in its headers and toolbar bulk actions. The rows are unfiltered and unselected, filter menus are closed, and no bulk action has been applied.
never: A Priority filter checklist already open
Only High or Urgent tickets already visible
Rows already selected for a bulk action

arrangements.text: Bulk actions sit above the ticket table, and value-filter controls sit in its headers.
Bulk actions sit above the right end of the table, while filter controls remain beside their column labels.

scenarios.name: virtual
scenarios.screen: A ticket table shows a scrollable window of rows from a longer record list, with columns that include editable values such as Owner. The window starts at the top of the list, and no cell editor is open.
never: Every record rendered as a row at once
The table already scrolled to the target record
An Owner cell already in edit mode
A new cell value already entered

arrangements.text: Headers sit above a scrollable row viewport, with the first records visible beneath them.
Table controls sit above the right end of the grid; the scrollable row viewport remains directly below the headers.
